title: Blood Feeding Protocol for Aedes aegypti
author: Steven Stenhouse
materials: Use a thermometer to monitor the blood temperature. The blood is ready for use when it reaches 45–48 °C.

steps.title: Store blood refrigerated
steps.instruction: Keep defibrinated sheep blood refrigerated until ready for use.

steps.title: Set up water recirculator
steps.instruction: Attach the jacketed beaker to the inlet and outlet tubes of the heated water recirculator, fill the recirculator with water, close the lid, plug in the machine, set the temperature to 48 °C, check for air bubbles in the recirculator, jacketed beaker, and tubing, start the pump, open the port and add water as needed to maintain consistent flow and volume.

steps.title: Prepare and clean watch glasses
steps.instruction: Wrap each watch glass with a 25 cm² piece of parafilm using a cup as a support; stretch the parafilm taut across the top, secure it to the underside, leaving a small opening for pipetting. Place the wrapped glasses in a sink, turn on tap water, peel off the parafilm into a trash container, remove any clotted blood or residue with gloves, rinse thoroughly, soak the glasses in a 1:100 dilution of 6 % bleach solution for approximately 2 hours, rinse again with tap water, and air‑dry.

steps.title: Heat blood to feeding temperature
steps.instruction: Pour the calculated total volume of defibrinated sheep blood (≈8 mL per watch glass) into the jacketed beaker, heat with the recirculator until the blood reaches 38 °C, confirming the temperature with an infrared thermometer.

steps.title: Measure blood aliquots
steps.instruction: Using a graduated pipette, measure 8 mL of the warmed blood for each watch glass.

steps.title: Load blood into watch glasses
steps.instruction: Hold each watch glass vertically with the parafilm opening upward, pipette 8 mL of blood into the pocket (filling about half), gently tilt the glass forward and press the parafilm with the thumb to expel excess air, then seal the parafilm to the back of the glass.

steps.title: Position watch glasses on heat pads
steps.instruction: Connect heat pads to the temperature‑controlled heating unit using appropriate hooks and plugs; the unit should provide stable, uniform heat approximating host body temperature. Place each prepared watch glass (parafilm‑side up) flat on the pads, ensure no leaks and that blood contacts most of the parafilm surface.

steps.title: Insert feeding devices into cages
steps.instruction: Place one blood‑feeding device (containing a prepared watch glass) in each mosquito cage for up to 24 hours, inspect devices periodically, and monitor blood temperature with an infrared thermometer to keep it at 38 °C throughout the feeding period.

steps.title: Post‑feeding cleanup
steps.instruction: After feeding, carefully remove each device, blow on it to dislodge as many females as possible, separate heating sources from the watch glasses, place blood‑containing materials in a plastic tray, and transport them to the wash area.
